1. Neutralization is a way to go neutral in dollar sense, i.e. allotting the same amount of dollars in long (buying) and short (selling) positions. Hence your total investment will be split down the middle – half for short and half for long. That way, you are less exposed to risk, when the entire market goes up or down.

Neutralization is a vital risk management technique in quant trading, ensuring equal allocation of dollars to long and short positions. This balanced approach minimizes exposure to market-wide movements, making strategies more robust against systemic trends.

Neutralization is indeed a technique used in quantitative trading to reduce or eliminate certain risks by balancing the long and short positions. The goal is to create a portfolio where the long and short positions offset each other, ensuring that the overall exposure to market movements is minimized.
